finding.claim: Authorization identity is taken from the client-controlled X-Session-User-Verified header with no verification, letting any directly reachable caller act as any granted user and delete or rename files they should not control.
finding.source: HTTP request header X-Session-User-Verified, read verbatim in load_user (views.py:10-11) and placed in g.user.
finding.sink: ensure_allowed(g.user, f, "delete") at views.py:17 guarding del STORE[fid] at views.py:18; is_allowed(g.user, f, "write") at views.py:25 guarding f["name"] assignment at views.py:27.

trace.note: before_request load_user runs on every request with no session, token, or signature check.
g.user = request.headers.get("X-Session-User-Verified") copies the client-supplied value directly.
delete_file loads f = STORE[fid] for the attacker-chosen fid.
ensure_allowed(g.user, f, "delete") trusts the spoofed identity.
is_allowed returns True when grants[g.user] contains "delete", so the spoofed name passes.
del STORE[fid] executes, removing the file.

finding.guards_checked: before_request performs no authentication; ensure_allowed/is_allowed are correct for the identity they receive but cannot detect spoofing; no auth middleware, reverse-proxy header stripping, or session binding exists in the repo; rename and delete are not cookie-authenticated so CSRF does not apply. Exploitability depends on deployment: not exploitable if a trusted proxy strips inbound X-Session-User-Verified and sets it only after authenticating the session, which the repo does not show.

verdict.guard_found: None effective in the repo. views.py:9-11 (before_request) only copies the header with no authentication, signature, or session check. acl.py:4-10 checks are correct for whatever identity they receive. ensure_allowed (views.py:17) is a bare call, but it aborts with 403 on failure (acl.py:10), so it is not discarded. is_allowed at views.py:25 is tested. Any upstream proxy that strips or sets the header is outside the repo and unverified.
verdict.reason: views.py:11 takes g.user verbatim from the X-Session-User-Verified request header with no verification, and acl.py:5 grants delete/write based on that value, so any caller who can reach the service and knows a file id and a grantee name can delete (views.py:18) or rename (views.py:27) the file. The only residual doubt is an upstream proxy that the repo does not show; the code as written has no trust boundary.
